parsed.explanation: Claim 3.2's proof forms the integer π(T) from a minimal transversal T of C; π is defined only for finite prime sets, and nothing in the text shows minimal transversals of C are finite (members of C are finite, but transversals need not be). So hypothesis (iii) is proved only for finite T. Step 4's final use applies (iii) to a minimal transversal inside the infinite set I ∪ Z_ω and then infers 'Since T is finite' from T ∈ C — exactly the unproved case. The Case A use (inside the finite I ∪ Z_s) is fine, but the terminal contradiction, and hence the finiteness/large-prime-erasure content (L6.2), is not established.
